items.title: Meta’s Muse Charm might cost $300
items.excerpt: Meta's upcoming Muse Charm AI wearable may cost about $300 and could come with a 12-month 5G data plan, per The Information; Meta says it will have more to share soon.

items.title: Meta's new Muse Charm device may cost $300
items.excerpt: Alternate source for the Muse Charm pricing story: Meta hasn't denied The Information's report and says it will 'have more to share soon' about its upcoming AI wearable.

items.title: Pebble Index 01 AI ring review: When a single feature becomes the product
items.excerpt: Engadget reviews Pebble's Index 01 AI ring (8/10): it does one thing, is cheap and low-tech, but the reviewer found it very useful. Downsides noted: imperfect AI and a non-rechargeable battery.

items.title: OpenAI is apparently serious about an AI phone, as report claims production order has been placed
items.excerpt: China's Securities Times reports that Foxconn subsidiary FIH Mobile has received an order to help assemble a smartphone for OpenAI, suggesting the ChatGPT maker's first phone is moving toward production.

items.title: OpenAI's first smartphone could launch in 2027 with help from iPhone manufacturer
items.excerpt: Alternate source for the OpenAI phone story: the report says Foxconn secured an assembly order and puts launch in late 2027 or 2028.

items.title: First look at Nothing's AI gadget shared ahead of launch
items.excerpt: A first look shows the design of Nothing's dedicated AI device, which CEO Carl Pei teased earlier this month, along with hints at possible features. It joins the Humane AI Pin and Rabbit R1 category of dedicated AI gadgets.

items.title: Nothing’s first AI gadget appears in real ahead of its December launch, and it has a big Talk button
items.excerpt: Alternate source for the Nothing device leak: a photo shows a screenless AI device with a Talk button, a record button and status lights, weeks before its December launch.

items.title: Nothing’s upcoming AI gadget just leaked, with two buttons and more mystery
items.excerpt: Alternate source for the Nothing leak: the image shows two buttons on the device but makes its purpose no clearer.

items.title: Samsung prepares Galaxy AI on Snapdragon X Elite for its upcoming Android laptops
items.excerpt: An APK teardown of the One UI 9.5 beta shows Samsung preparing on-device Galaxy AI photo tools, its Gauss language model and 8K video tools for Android laptops running Snapdragon X Elite.

items.title: Scout Motors Is Using AI Earpieces to Train Factory Workers
items.excerpt: Scout Motors is replacing the instruction binder with AI earpieces whose voice walks new hires through hands-on tasks. The automaker sees the same approach reaching service centers and, eventually, owners' garages.

items.title: 파리로엠엔비, AI로 맥박 맞춰 자극 조절하는 헤드밴드 '뉴라온 어시스트' CES 2027서 첫 공개
items.excerpt: Healthcare startup Paryrom&B will debut Neuraon Assist at CES 2027. The AI wellness headband reads pulse changes in real time and adjusts the transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation it delivers through contacts at the ear.

items.title: [포토] 샤오미, AI 후면 디스플레이 탑재 신제품 국내 출시
items.excerpt: Xiaomi Korea has officially launched the Xiaomi 18 Pro Max in Korea, a flagship with an AI rear display and Leica dual 200MP cameras (alternate/Korean angle for the Xiaomi 18 Pro launch).

items.title: Xiaomi's 18 Pro series can generate vibe-coded apps for its tiny rear display
items.excerpt: At the Xiaomi 18 Pro series global launch, Engadget went hands-on with the rear second screen, which can run vibe-coded mini apps generated with AI, alongside the cameras and a new red color.

items.title: Successor to well-reviewed Switchbot AI Art Frame unveiled with upgraded features for art and photo lovers
items.excerpt: SwitchBot has released the AI Art Frame 2 (AI Art Canvas in Japan), a color E Ink frame. Its AI 'Weather Muse' changes the art to match the forecast, and a $3.99/month subscription adds voice-, text- and image-to-image AI art generation.

items.title: Xreal Aura Review: Android XR combined with lightweight glasses delivers a true next-gen spatial computing experience
items.excerpt: Tom's Hardware reviews the $1,099 Xreal Aura Android XR glasses. A puck powered by Qualcomm's Snapdragon Reality Elite (48 TOPS of AI compute) drives them, and they ship with a controller that has a Gemini button. (Smart-glasses cap 1: shipping review)

items.title: Flowtica Reveals Verso MagSafe AI Recorder With E-Ink Display
items.excerpt: Flowtica's Verso is a MagSafe AI voice recorder with a low-power E Ink screen that updates continuously during calls, meetings and voice memos. Preorders are open. (Off-list: no allowed-domain coverage found)

items.title: AceiiLab's tennis robot rallies back, roams the baseline, and folds into your trunk
items.excerpt: The AceiiLab A1 tennis robot rolls along the baseline, watches your shots and returns them. After each session its AI coach reports a weakness analysis, training suggestions and progress tracking.
